title: Python for Everybody
author: Charles Severance
about: Severance's introduction to programming, built from his University of Michigan course and given away free online. It teaches Python through working with real data rather than abstract exercises, which makes it one of the gentler ways in.

title: Python Crash Course
author: Eric Matthes
about: A fast, project-driven introduction. The first half covers the language; the second builds three real things: a game, a data visualization and a web application.

title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python + Workbook
author: Al Sweigart
about: Python for people who want to get something done: renaming files, filling spreadsheets, scraping pages, sending email. Sweigart teaches the language through the chores it can take off your hands, and the workbook adds practice for each chapter.

title: Fluent Python
author: Luciano Ramalho
about: For programmers who already know Python and want to write it the way the language intends. Ramalho works through the data model, iterators, generators and concurrency, explaining the design decisions underneath the features.

title: Powerful Python
author: Aaron Maxwell
about: An intermediate book on the patterns experienced Python developers lean on: generators, decorators, higher-order functions and test-driven development.

title: Python Cookbook
about: Recipes for specific problems, each worked through with an explanation of why the solution works. Less a book to read in order than one to open when you are stuck.

title: High Performance Python
author: Micha Gorelick & Ian Ozsvald
about: How to find out why Python code is slow and what to do about it: profiling, NumPy, compiled extensions, concurrency and clusters. Measurement first, optimization second.

title: Python Testing with pytest
author: Brian Okken
about: A practical guide to pytest, the testing framework most Python projects now use. Fixtures, parametrization and plugins, explained through a small working project.

title: Think Like a Programmer
author: V. Anton Spraul
about: Not a language book but a problem-solving one. Spraul argues that the hard part of programming is breaking a problem down, and teaches that skill directly.

title: Django for Beginners
author: William Vincent
about: A step-by-step introduction to Django that builds several complete projects, from a single page to a newspaper site with user accounts, and deploys each one.

title: Django for APIs
author: William Vincent
about: The companion volume, focused on building web APIs with Django REST Framework: serialization, permissions, authentication and documentation.

title: Django 5 by Example
author: Antonio Melé
about: A project-based tour of Django, building a blog, a social site, an online shop and an e-learning platform, each introducing more of the framework.

title: Two Scoops of Django
author: Daniel and Audrey Feldroy
about: A book of best practices rather than a tutorial: how experienced Django developers structure projects, settings, models and deployments, and the mistakes they learned to avoid.

title: Learning Web Design
author: Jennifer Robbins
about: A ground-up introduction to building websites with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and web graphics, written for people with no background. Clear enough to be the first book in many courses.

title: Web Scraping with Python
author: Ryan Mitchell
about: How to collect data from the web programmatically, from parsing HTML to handling forms, logins and JavaScript-heavy sites, along with the legal and ethical questions that come with it.

title: Learning SQL
author: Alan Beaulieu
about: A clear introduction to SQL that goes beyond basic queries into joins, subqueries, grouping and transactions, with attention to how databases actually process what you write.

title: SQL Cookbook
author: Anthony Molinaro
about: Solutions to the queries people actually struggle with, shown side by side across several database systems. Useful for seeing that one problem can be solved more than one way.

title: Python for Data Analysis
author: Wes McKinney
about: Written by the creator of pandas, the working manual for cleaning, reshaping and analyzing data in Python, with NumPy and Jupyter alongside.

title: Storytelling with Data
author: Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic
about: On making charts people understand. Knaflic, who taught data visualization at Google, shows how to cut clutter, direct attention and build a narrative around a number.

title: Data Science for Business
author: Foster Provost & Tom Fawcett
about: The concepts behind data science explained for people who make decisions with it: what the methods can and cannot tell you, and how to treat data as a business asset.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
about: The book engineers pass around for understanding how data systems really work: replication, partitioning, transactions, consistency and the trade-offs between them. Dense, careful and widely regarded as the best of its kind.

title: Fundamentals of Data Engineering
author: Joe Reis & Matt Housley
about: An overview of the data engineering lifecycle, from ingestion to serving, written to outlast any particular tool.

title: Microsoft Excel Data Analysis and Business Modeling
author: Wayne Winston
about: A practical course in using Excel for real analysis: forecasting, optimization, simulation and financial modeling, taught through business problems.

title: Naked Statistics
author: Charles Wheelan
about: Statistics explained without the formulas getting in the way. Wheelan focuses on intuition: what a number is really saying, and the ways it can mislead.

title: The Manga Guide to Statistics
author: Shin Takahashi
about: Statistics taught through a comic-book story. An unlikely format that makes the core ideas easier to hold on to.

title: The Manga Guide to Linear Algebra
author: Shin Takahashi & Iroha Inoue
about: Vectors, matrices and transformations through a manga narrative, with worked problems behind the story.

title: The Manga Guide to Calculus
author: Hiroyuki Kojima
about: Derivatives and integrals introduced through a story, grounding each idea in a practical situation before the notation arrives.

title: Essential Math for Data Science
author: Thomas Nield
about: The mathematics underneath data science and machine learning, from probability and statistics to linear algebra and calculus, explained for working programmers.

title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
author: Marc Peter Deisenroth, A. Aldo Faisal & Cheng Soon Ong
about: A rigorous bridge between undergraduate mathematics and machine learning: linear algebra, geometry, probability and optimization, then the models built on them.

title: Practical Statistics for Data Scientists
author: Peter Bruce, Andrew Bruce & Peter Gedeck
about: The statistical concepts that matter most in data science, with a clear eye on which classical methods still earn their place and which do not.

title: Math for Programmers
author: Paul Orland
about: Mathematics taught through code: vectors, calculus and machine learning built up in Python rather than on paper.

title: Data Science from Scratch
author: Joel Grus
about: Grus builds the tools of data science himself in plain Python, from statistics to neural networks, so the reader sees what the libraries are actually doing.

title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras & TensorFlow
author: Aurélien Géron
about: The standard practical guide to machine learning in Python, moving from classical methods with Scikit-Learn to deep learning with Keras and TensorFlow.

title: StatQuest Illustrated Guide to Neural Networks and AI
author: Josh Starmer
about: Starmer's visual, step-by-step explanation of how neural networks work, in the same friendly style as his StatQuest videos.

title: Practical Deep Learning for Cloud, Mobile and Edge
author: Howard & Gugger

title: Natural Language Processing with Transformers
author: Lewis Tunstall, Leandro von Werra & Thomas Wolf
about: Written by engineers at Hugging Face, a practical guide to transformer models for classification, generation, summarization and question answering.

title: Build a Large Language Model from Scratch
author: Sebastian Raschka
about: Raschka builds a GPT-style language model step by step in PyTorch, from tokenization and attention to pretraining and fine-tuning.

title: AI Engineering
author: Chip Huyen
about: How to build applications on foundation models: evaluation, prompt engineering, retrieval, fine-tuning and the systems around them.

title: Generative AI Design Patterns
author: Valliappa Lakshmanan & Hannes Hapke
about: A catalogue of recurring solutions for building with generative AI, in the tradition of design patterns books for software.

title: Building Data-Driven Applications with LlamaIndex
author: Andrei Gheorghiu
about: A guide to retrieval-augmented generation with LlamaIndex, connecting language models to your own documents and data.

title: Natural Language Processing with Python
author: Steven Bird, Ewan Klein & Edward Loper
about: The book behind NLTK, introducing natural language processing through hands-on work with real text.

title: Building Machine Learning Powered Applications
author: Emmanuel Ameisen
about: The whole path from product idea to deployed machine learning model, with as much attention on iteration and debugging as on the models themselves.

title: Clean Code
author: Robert C. Martin
about: Martin's argument that code is read far more often than it is written, and his rules for making it readable. Influential, and argued with as much as followed.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: Andrew Hunt & David Thomas
about: Advice on the craft of software development, from debugging to working habits. Its phrases, like DRY and tracer bullets, entered the everyday vocabulary of the field.

title: A Philosophy of Software Design
author: John Ousterhout
about: Ousterhout's case that the central problem in software is complexity, and that good design means deep modules behind simple interfaces. A short book that takes issue with some popular advice.

title: Modern Software Engineering
author: David Farley
about: Farley argues for treating software development as a genuine engineering discipline, built on learning and managing complexity rather than following fashion.

title: Architecture Patterns with Python
author: Harry Percival & Bob Gregory
about: Domain-driven design, event-driven architecture and related patterns, translated into idiomatic Python.

title: Design Patterns
author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson & John Vlissides
about: The catalogue of twenty-three object-oriented design patterns that gave the field a shared vocabulary. Known everywhere as the Gang of Four book.

title: Fundamentals of Software Architecture
author: Mark Richards & Neal Ford
about: A broad introduction to the architect's job: architectural styles, the characteristics they trade off, and the soft skills the role demands.

title: Software Architecture: The Hard Parts
author: Neal Ford, Mark Richards, Pramod Sadalage & Zhamak Dehghani
about: Follows a fictional team through the hardest decisions in distributed architecture, where every choice is a trade-off and there is rarely a best answer.

title: Building Microservices
author: Sam Newman
about: The standard reference on designing, deploying and running systems built from small independent services, including when not to.

title: System Design Interview
author: Alex Xu & Sahn Lam
about: Worked walkthroughs of designing large systems, from rate limiters to chat services. Written for interview preparation, but a good tour of how real systems are built.

title: Generative AI System Design Interview
author: Ali Aminian & Hao Sheng
about: The same approach applied to generative AI: how to design and reason about products built on large models.

title: Computer Science: An Interdisciplinary Approach
author: Robert Sedgewick & Kevin Wayne
about: Princeton's introductory computer science course in book form, covering programming, algorithms, the theory of computation and machine architecture.

title: The Algorithm Design Manual
author: Steven Skiena
about: Half textbook, half catalogue of algorithmic problems, with Skiena's war stories about applying them. A practitioner's book rather than a theorist's.

title: Grokking Algorithms
author: Aditya Bhargava
about: An illustrated introduction to common algorithms, drawn rather than proved, for readers who find the standard textbooks hard going.

title: Cracking the Coding Interview
author: Gayle Laakmann McDowell
about: The standard preparation book for technical interviews: programming questions with worked solutions and a guide to how the process works from the inside.

title: Hacker's Delight
author: Henry S. Warren Jr.
about: A collection of bit manipulation tricks and low-level arithmetic techniques, the kind of cleverness that lives inside compilers and hardware.

title: The Art of Computer Programming
author: Donald Knuth
about: Knuth's multivolume analysis of algorithms, begun in the 1960s and still in progress. The foundational work of the field, and famously demanding.

title: Black Hat Python
author: Justin Seitz
about: Python for offensive security: writing your own network tools and exploits to understand how attacks actually work.

title: Hacking: The Art of Exploitation
author: Jon Erickson
about: Exploitation taught from first principles: C, assembly, memory, networking and how vulnerabilities arise. Comes with an environment to practice in.

title: Penetration Testing
author: Georgia Weidman
about: A hands-on introduction to penetration testing, built around a lab the reader sets up to practice the full process safely.

title: The Web Application Hacker's Handbook
author: Dafydd Stuttard & Marcus Pinto
about: A thorough manual of how web applications are attacked, by the creator of Burp Suite. For years the standard reference for web security testing.

title: The Hacker Playbook
author: Peter Kim
about: Kim's field manuals for penetration testing, organized like a sports playbook around the phases of a real engagement.

title: Pro Git
author: Scott Chacon & Ben Straub
about: The comprehensive guide to Git, free to read online, covering daily use and the internals underneath.

title: The Linux Command Line
author: William Shotts
about: A complete introduction to the shell, from first commands to writing scripts. Patient enough to take someone from nervous to fluent.

title: Practical Vim
author: Drew Neil
about: Organized as tips rather than a tutorial, each one a small lesson in thinking the way Vim wants you to.

title: Mastering Vim
author: Ruslan Osipov
about: Building an efficient Vim setup: navigation, plugins, configuration and customization for serious daily use.

title: React Native in Action
author: Nader Dabit
about: Building cross-platform mobile apps with React Native, from the fundamentals of the framework to navigation, animation and platform APIs.

title: Flutter for Beginners
author: Thomas Bailey & Alessandro Biessek
about: An introduction to Flutter and Dart for building mobile apps from a single codebase.

title: Flutter Complete Reference 2.0
author: Alberto Miola
about: A detailed reference to Dart and Flutter, covering the language in depth before moving to the framework.

subsection: How machines work — the history and theory shelf
title: Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
author: Charles Petzold
about: How computers work, built up from flashlights and telegraph relays to logic gates, memory and a working processor. One of the best explanations of the machine ever written for a general reader.

subsection: How machines work — the history and theory shelf
title: The Annotated Turing
author: Charles Petzold
about: Turing's 1936 paper on computable numbers, reproduced in full and explained line by line, with the mathematics and history needed to follow it.

subsection: How machines work — the history and theory shelf
title: Turing's Vision
author: Chris Bernhardt
about: A readable account of Turing's 1936 paper and the ideas it opened up: computability, decidability and the limits of what machines can do.

subsection: How machines work — the history and theory shelf
title: The Innovators
author: Walter Isaacson
about: A history of the digital revolution told through the people who built it, from Ada Lovelace to the founders of the internet, with an emphasis on collaboration over lone genius.

subsection: How machines work — the history and theory shelf
title: Leonardo da Vinci
author: Walter Isaacson
about: A biography built largely from Leonardo's notebooks, portraying a man driven by curiosity across art, engineering and anatomy.

title: Boolean algebra, programmed-instruction volume
author: Gerhard Hoernes & Melvin Heilweil
about: A programmed-instruction text that teaches Boolean algebra and logic design one small step at a time, with the reader answering as they go.

title: Digital Fundamentals
author: Thomas Floyd
about: A long-running textbook on digital electronics: number systems, logic gates, combinational and sequential circuits, and the building blocks of computers.

title: Boolean Algebra and Its Applications
author: J. Eldon Whitesitt
about: A short, clear introduction to Boolean algebra and its use in switching circuits and logic, kept in print for decades.

title: Digital Computer Electronics
author: Albert Malvino
about: Malvino builds a simple computer in stages, the SAP series, to show how digital circuits combine into a working machine. Many engineers first understood computers this way.

title: Make: Electronics
author: Charles Platt
about: Learning electronics by doing it: a series of experiments with real components, each explaining what happened and why.

title: Make: More Electronics
author: Charles Platt
about: The follow-up, moving into chips, sensors and more ambitious projects.

title: Encyclopedia of Electronic Components
author: Charles Platt
about: A reference to what components are, how they work and how they fail, organized for looking things up at the bench.

title: Practical Electronics for Inventors
author: Paul Scherz
about: A large, practical reference covering theory, components and circuit design, written for people who build things.

title: Physical Computing
author: Dan O'Sullivan & Tom Igoe
about: Using microcontrollers to connect computers to the physical world through sensors and motors. A foundational text of the maker movement.

title: Making Things Talk
author: Tom Igoe
about: Projects that get devices communicating with each other and with the internet.

title: Ingenious Mechanisms for Designers and Inventors
author: Franklin D. Jones (ed.)
about: A catalogue of mechanical devices drawn from industry, from cams and linkages to feeding and ejecting mechanisms. Solutions engineers have returned to for decades.

title: Product Design and Development
author: Karl Ulrich & Steven Eppinger
about: The standard textbook on how products move from concept to production, treating design as a process that can be managed.

title: Design for Manufacturability
author: David Anderson
about: How to design products so they can be built well and cheaply, making manufacturing a design constraint from the start.

title: Poorly Made in China
author: Paul Midler
about: An insider's account of manufacturing in southern China, and of how quality quietly erodes when a factory holds the advantage over its client.

title: The Goal
author: Eliyahu Goldratt
about: A business novel about a failing factory that introduces the theory of constraints: find the bottleneck, because everything else is secondary to it.

title: The Hardware Hacker
author: Andrew "bunnie" Huang
about: Essays from a hardware engineer on manufacturing in Shenzhen, reverse engineering and open hardware.

title: The Hardware Startup
author: Renee DiResta, Brady Forrest & Ryan Vinyard
about: A guide to taking a physical product from prototype to market: funding, manufacturing and distribution.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: Computer Power and Human Reason
author: Joseph Weizenbaum
about: Weizenbaum built ELIZA, then watched people confide in it. This is his argument that some decisions should never be handed to computers, however capable they become.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: Islands in the Cyberstream
author: Joseph Weizenbaum & Gunna Wendt
about: A late conversation with Weizenbaum, looking back on computing and society after decades of arguing against its excesses.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: The Technological Condition: An Anthology
author: Scharff & Dusek (eds.)
about: A broad anthology of the philosophy of technology, from the ancient Greeks through Heidegger to contemporary debates.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: The Question Concerning Technology and Other Essays
author: Martin Heidegger
about: Heidegger's essays arguing that modern technology is not just a set of tools but a way of revealing the world, one that turns everything, people included, into resources on standby.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: Technological Slavery
author: Theodore Kaczynski
about: Kaczynski's collected writings on why he considered industrial technology incompatible with human freedom. Read as the document of an argument and of the violence it was used to justify.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: Genius Makers
author: Cade Metz
about: A reported history of the researchers behind the deep learning revolution and the companies that competed to hire them.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: Amusing Ourselves to Death
author: Neil Postman
about: Postman's argument that television turned public discourse into entertainment, and that a culture can be undone by what it loves rather than what it fears.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
author: Shoshana Zuboff
about: Zuboff's account of an economic order built on extracting and predicting human behavior, and what it costs in autonomy.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: What Computers Still Can't Do
author: Hubert Dreyfus
about: Dreyfus's philosophical critique of symbolic AI, drawing on Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty to argue that human intelligence depends on embodied, situated know-how.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
author: Douglas Hofstadter
about: Hofstadter weaves Gödel's incompleteness, Escher's drawings and Bach's canons into an inquiry into how meaning and self-reference arise from formal systems. It won the Pulitzer Prize.

subsection: Computers, AI, and the human question
title: The Sciences of the Artificial
author: Herbert Simon
about: Simon's lectures on the design of artificial systems, from economies and organizations to minds, and the idea of bounded rationality.

title: I and Thou
author: Martin Buber
about: Buber's short, dense work distinguishing two ways of meeting the world: as an It to be used, or as a Thou to be encountered.

title: Existentialism Is a Humanism
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
edition: Yale University Press, translated by Carol Macomber
about: Sartre's 1945 lecture defending existentialism to a general audience, and the source of the claim that existence precedes essence.

title: Being and Time
author: Martin Heidegger
edition: Translated by John Macquarrie and Edward Robinson
about: Heidegger's unfinished masterwork on the question of what it means to be, approached through human existence. Macquarrie and Robinson's is the long-standard English version.

title: The Myth of Sisyphus
author: Albert Camus
about: Camus's essay on the absurd and on whether life is worth living without ultimate meaning. It ends by imagining Sisyphus happy at his rock.

title: Man's Search for Meaning
author: Viktor Frankl
about: Frankl's account of surviving the Nazi camps, followed by an outline of logotherapy, built on the claim that meaning can be found even in suffering.

title: The Denial of Death
author: Ernest Becker
about: Becker's Pulitzer-winning argument that much of human culture is a defense against the knowledge that we will die.

title: Discourses, Fragments, Handbook
author: Epictetus
edition: Oxford World's Classics, translated by Robin Hard
about: The teachings of a former slave turned Stoic teacher, recorded by his student Arrian. The Handbook distills them into a manual for separating what is in our power from what is not.

title: Letters from a Stoic
author: Seneca
about: Seneca's letters to Lucilius: practical reflections on time, friendship, wealth and death. The most personal and readable of the Roman Stoics.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
about: Private notes an emperor wrote to himself, never meant for publication. A record of someone trying, daily, to live by Stoic principles under enormous pressure.

title: Courage Under Fire
author: James Stockdale
about: Stockdale's lecture on how Epictetus helped him endure seven and a half years as a prisoner of war in Vietnam.

title: Cyropaedia
author: Xenophon
edition: Cornell University Press, translated by Wayne Ambler
about: Xenophon's idealized account of the education and rule of Cyrus the Great, part biography and part treatise on leadership. Machiavelli read it closely.

title: Elements
author: Euclid
about: Geometry built from a handful of definitions and axioms into a complete system. For over two thousand years the model of what rigorous reasoning looks like.

title: The Prince
author: Niccolò Machiavelli
edition: Penguin Classics, translated by George Bull
about: A short treatise on acquiring and keeping power, written in 1513 and published after Machiavelli's death. Its reputation is darker than its argument, which is about how politics works rather than how it ought to.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
about: The ancient Chinese treatise on strategy, built on the idea that the best victory is the one won without fighting.

title: The Complete Musashi
author: Miyamoto Musashi
about: Musashi's writings, including The Book of Five Rings, on strategy, swordsmanship and the discipline of a warrior's path.

title: Hagakure
author: Yamamoto Tsunetomo
about: Reflections of an eighteenth-century samurai retainer on duty, death and loyalty, recorded by a younger listener. Famous and often misread.

title: On War
author: Carl von Clausewitz
edition: Princeton University Press, translated by Michael Howard and Peter Paret
about: Clausewitz's unfinished study of war as the continuation of politics, full of friction, chance and fog. The Howard and Paret translation is the standard.

title: The Strategy of Conflict
author: Thomas Schelling
about: Schelling applies game theory to bargaining, deterrence and conflict, showing how commitment and focal points shape outcomes. Part of the work that won him a Nobel prize.

title: Strategy
author: B. H. Liddell Hart
about: Liddell Hart's survey of military history arguing for the indirect approach: winning by dislocating the opponent rather than meeting strength with strength.

title: Boyd
author: Robert Coram
about: A biography of John Boyd, the fighter pilot and strategist behind the OODA loop, and of the institutions he fought as fiercely as any opponent.

title: The Art of Worldly Wisdom
author: Baltasar Gracián
about: Three hundred aphorisms from a seventeenth-century Jesuit on prudence, reputation and dealing with people. Sharp, worldly and still quoted.

title: Logically Fallacious
author: Bo Bennett
about: A reference to more than three hundred logical fallacies, each defined and illustrated with examples.

title: Being Logical
author: D. Q. McInerny
about: A short, plain guide to reasoning well: clear thinking, the structure of arguments and how they go wrong.

title: An Illustrated Book of Bad Arguments
author: Ali Almossawi
about: Common fallacies explained through illustrated animal scenes. Brief, charming and surprisingly precise.

title: The Hebrew Bible
author: Robert Alter
about: Alter's translation of the entire Hebrew Bible with commentary, completed over more than two decades and aiming to keep the literary force of the original.

title: Tanakh
author: Jewish Publication Society
about: The Jewish Publication Society translation of the Hebrew Bible, the standard English version in many Jewish communities.

title: Tales of the Hasidim
author: Martin Buber
about: Buber's retelling of the stories of the Hasidic masters, gathered and shaped over many years.

title: Tales of the Dervishes
author: Idries Shah
about: Teaching stories from the Sufi tradition, meant to be read more than once and to work on the reader over time.

title: The Sabbath
author: Abraham Joshua Heschel
about: Heschel's meditation on the Sabbath as a sanctuary in time rather than space. Short, lyrical and one of the defining works of twentieth-century Jewish thought.

title: God: A Biography
author: Jack Miles
about: Miles reads God as the protagonist of the Hebrew Bible, following the character through the text as a literary critic would. It won the Pulitzer Prize.

title: Physician of the Soul, Healer of the Cosmos
author: Lawrence Fine
about: A study of Isaac Luria and the circle of kabbalists around him in sixteenth-century Safed.

title: Sha'ar HaGilgulim
author: Chaim Vital
edition: Vol. 1, digital edition, translated by Winston
about: The Gate of Reincarnations, a central text of Lurianic kabbalah as recorded by Luria's disciple Chaim Vital.

title: The Jewish Annotated New Testament
author: Amy-Jill Levine & Marc Zvi Brettler (eds.)
about: The New Testament annotated by Jewish scholars, reading the texts in the context of the Judaism they came from.

title: A River Flows from Eden
author: Melila Hellner-Eshed
about: A study of the Zohar as living mystical experience rather than doctrine alone, attending to its language and its circle of companions.

title: The Hero with a Thousand Faces
author: Joseph Campbell
about: Campbell's comparative study of myth and the pattern he called the monomyth, the hero's journey. Enormously influential on storytelling well beyond scholarship.

title: The Times Complete History of the World
author: Richard Overy (ed.)
about: World history told through maps, from the earliest humans to the present.

title: The Penguin History of the World
author: J. M. Roberts & Odd Arne Westad
about: A single-volume world history, revised and extended by Westad. Wide in scope and unusually readable for its size.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
about: Harari's sweeping account of how Homo sapiens came to dominate the planet through cognitive, agricultural and scientific revolutions. Widely read and widely argued with.

title: The Lessons of History
author: Will & Ariel Durant
about: A short distillation of the Durants' decades on The Story of Civilization, asking what history teaches about human nature, government and war.

title: The Dawn of Everything
author: David Graeber & David Wengrow
about: An anthropologist and an archaeologist challenge the standard story of social evolution, arguing that early societies experimented with far more political arrangements than we assume.

title: These Truths
author: Jill Lepore
about: A single-volume history of the United States, organized around whether the country has lived up to its founding claims.

title: Land of Hope
author: Wilfred McClay
about: A narrative history of the United States, written for students and general readers as a counterweight to more critical accounts.

title: The PayPal Wars
author: Eric Jackson
about: An early PayPal employee's account of the company's fights with eBay, regulators and fraudsters, and of the team that later scattered across Silicon Valley.

title: Bicentennial illustrated history set (decorative rather than scholarly)
Rubicon
author: Tom Holland
about: A narrative history of the fall of the Roman Republic, from its expansion to the civil wars that ended it, told with a novelist's pace.

title: Lives
author: Plutarch
about: Plutarch's paired biographies of Greek and Roman statesmen, written to examine character rather than events. Shakespeare drew on them heavily.

title: Selected Works
author: Cicero
edition: Penguin Classics, translated by Michael Grant
about: Cicero's speeches, letters and philosophical writing in one volume: the orator, the politician and the thinker together.

title: Selected Political Speeches
author: Cicero
edition: Penguin Classics, translated by Michael Grant
about: Cicero at his most public, in speeches from the prosecutions and political crises of the late Republic.

title: SPQR
author: Mary Beard
about: Beard's history of Rome's first thousand years, skeptical of legend and attentive to how the Romans told their own story.

title: Jews vs. Rome: Two Centuries of Rebellion Against the World’s Mightiest Empire
author: Barry Strauss
about: The Jewish revolts against Rome, from the Great Revolt to Bar Kokhba, and their long consequences.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: Shahnameh
author: Ferdowsi
edition: Penguin Classics, translated by Dick Davis
about: The Persian Book of Kings, Ferdowsi's epic of Iran's mythical and historical past, completed around 1010. Davis renders it in a mix of prose and verse.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: A History of Iran: Empire of the Mind
author: Michael Axworthy
about: A history of Iran from antiquity to the present, arguing that Iranian identity has persisted through culture and ideas more than through borders.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: Two Centuries of Silence
author: Abdolhossein Zarrinkoub
about: A classic Persian history of the two centuries after the Arab conquest of Iran, and of how Persian language and identity survived them.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: Esther's Children: A Portrait of Iranian Jews
author: Houman Sarshar (ed.)
about: A richly illustrated portrait of the Jews of Iran and their history, culture and communities across more than two and a half millennia.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: The Jews of Arab Lands in Modern Times
author: Norman Stillman
about: A history, with primary documents, of Jewish communities across the Arab world in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: The Jews of Islam
author: Bernard Lewis
about: Lewis's study of Jewish life under Muslim rule from the beginnings of Islam to modern times.

subsection: Persia, Iran, and the Jewish world
title: Journey from the Land of No
author: Roya Hakakian
about: A memoir of growing up Jewish in Tehran through the Iranian revolution.

title: Endurance
author: Alfred Lansing
about: Shackleton's Antarctic expedition, in which the ship was crushed by ice and every man survived. Built from interviews and diaries.

title: Missing 411
author: David Paulides
about: Paulides's series collecting unexplained disappearances in national parks and wilderness areas.

title: The Red Book
author: C. G. Jung
about: Jung's private record of the visions he explored from 1913, illustrated in his own hand and unpublished until 2009.

title: Man and His Symbols
author: C. G. Jung
about: The one book Jung made for a general audience, with collaborators, explaining dreams, symbols and the unconscious.

title: Modern Man in Search of a Soul
author: C. G. Jung
about: Essays on dream analysis, the stages of life and the spiritual problem of modern people.

title: Synchronicity
author: C. G. Jung
about: Jung's essay on meaningful coincidences with no causal connection, developed partly in conversation with the physicist Wolfgang Pauli.

title: The Essential Jung: Selected Writings
author: Anthony Storr (ed.)
about: Storr's selection of Jung's writings, arranged to trace the development of his ideas.

title: The Freud/Jung Letters
author: William McGuire (ed.)
about: The complete correspondence between Freud and Jung, from their close alliance to the break that ended it.

title: The Freud Reader
author: Peter Gay (ed.)
about: A single-volume selection of Freud's writings, edited by his biographer, covering the full range of his work.

title: King, Warrior, Magician, Lover
author: Robert Moore & Douglas Gillette
about: A Jungian account of four archetypes of mature masculinity and the immature forms they take.

title: The Anatomy of Human Destructiveness
author: Erich Fromm
about: Fromm's study of human aggression, distinguishing defensive aggression from cruelty and destructiveness.

title: The Body Keeps the Score
author: Bessel van der Kolk
about: A psychiatrist's account of how trauma reshapes the body and brain, and of the treatments that help.

title: Feeling Good
author: David Burns
about: The book that brought cognitive behavioral therapy to general readers, teaching how to identify and challenge distorted thinking.

title: Influence
author: Robert Cialdini
about: Cialdini's study of the principles behind persuasion, such as reciprocity, social proof and scarcity, and how they are used on us.

title: Thinking in Bets
author: Annie Duke
about: A former professional poker player on deciding under uncertainty, and on separating the quality of a decision from the luck of its outcome.

title: The Worldly Philosophers
author: Robert Heilbroner
about: The lives and ideas of the great economists, from Adam Smith to Keynes and Schumpeter. For decades the book that drew people into economics.

title: The Wealth of Nations
author: Adam Smith
about: Smith's inquiry into what makes nations prosperous: the division of labor, markets and the limits of government. The founding text of modern economics.

title: Basic Economics
author: Thomas Sowell
about: Economics without graphs or equations, focused on incentives and consequences, especially the ones nobody intended.

title: A Conflict of Visions
author: Thomas Sowell
about: Sowell's argument that political disagreements trace back to two underlying views of human nature, which he calls the constrained and the unconstrained.

title: Black Rednecks and White Liberals
author: Thomas Sowell
about: Essays on cultural history, including Sowell's argument about the origins of certain cultural patterns in the American South.

title: Discrimination and Disparities
author: Thomas Sowell
about: Sowell examines why outcomes differ between groups and argues that discrimination is only one of many causes.

title: Capital in the Twenty-First Century
author: Thomas Piketty
about: Piketty's historical study of wealth and inequality, arguing that when returns on capital outpace growth, inequality tends to rise.

title: Capitalism and Freedom
author: Milton Friedman
about: Friedman's case that economic freedom is a precondition for political freedom, with proposals that have shaped policy debates ever since.

title: Capitalism, Socialism and Democracy
author: Joseph Schumpeter
about: Schumpeter's study of capitalism's dynamics and future, and the source of the idea of creative destruction.

title: Principles of Economics
author: N. Gregory Mankiw
about: Mankiw's widely used introductory textbook, organized around ten principles of economics.

title: Competitive Strategy
author: Michael Porter
about: Porter's framework for analyzing industries and competitors, including the five forces. A foundation of business strategy.

title: Good Strategy Bad Strategy
author: Richard Rumelt
about: Rumelt's argument that most of what passes for strategy is goals and slogans, and that real strategy starts with a diagnosis of the problem.

title: Positioning
author: Al Ries & Jack Trout
about: The classic case that marketing is a battle for a place in the customer's mind, not over product features.

title: Obviously Awesome
author: April Dunford
about: A practical method for product positioning, especially for products whose value customers do not immediately understand.

title: Purple Cow
author: Seth Godin
about: Godin's argument that in a crowded market only the remarkable gets noticed.

title: Play Bigger
author: Al Ramadan, Dave Peterson, Christopher Lochhead & Kevin Maney
about: On category design: the idea that the most successful companies create and define new markets rather than compete in existing ones.

title: Crossing the Chasm
author: Geoffrey Moore
about: Moore's account of the gap between early adopters and the mainstream market, and how technology companies get across it.

title: The Mom Test
author: Rob Fitzpatrick
about: How to talk to customers without being misled by politeness: ask about their lives and past behavior, not about your idea.

title: Running Lean
author: Ash Maurya
about: A step-by-step method for testing a business model before building too much of it.

title: The Startup Owner's Manual
author: Steve Blank & Bob Dorf
about: A detailed guide to customer development, the process of finding a repeatable business model by getting out of the building.

title: The SaaS Playbook
author: Rob Walling
about: Walling's guide to building a software business without venture capital, drawn from years of founding and investing in small SaaS companies.

title: Never Enough
author: Andrew Wilkinson
about: The founder of Tiny on building a holding company of internet businesses, and a candid account of what ambition cost him.

title: Rework
author: Jason Fried & David Heinemeier Hansson
about: The founders of Basecamp argue against much conventional business wisdom: growth for its own sake, long plans and workaholism.

title: Lean Analytics
author: Alistair Croll & Benjamin Yoskovitz
about: Which metrics matter at each stage of a startup, and how to use data to decide what to build next.

title: Traction
author: Gabriel Weinberg & Justin Mares
about: A framework for testing the channels through which a startup can find customers, with the argument that distribution deserves as much attention as product.

title: Lean B2B
author: Étienne Garbugli
about: Customer development adapted to selling to businesses, where buyers, users and decision makers are rarely the same person.

title: Subscribed
author: Tien Tzuo
about: The founder of Zuora on the shift from selling products to selling ongoing relationships, and what it demands of a company.

title: The Automatic Customer
author: John Warrillow
about: Subscription business models and why recurring revenue makes a company more valuable.

title: Demand-Side Sales
author: Bob Moesta
about: Sales seen from the buyer's side, using jobs to be done to understand the struggle that makes someone ready to buy.

title: Monetizing Innovation
author: Madhavan Ramanujam & Georg Tacke
about: The case for designing a product around what customers will pay, starting the pricing conversation before the product is built.

title: Hooked
author: Nir Eyal
about: Eyal's model of habit-forming products: trigger, action, variable reward, investment. Useful to builders, and a clear account of what the attention economy does to users.

title: Hacking Growth
author: Sean Ellis & Morgan Brown
about: A method for rapid experimentation across a product and its marketing, from the person who coined the term growth hacking.

title: The Art of SEO
author: Eric Enge, Stephan Spencer & Jessie Stricchiola
about: A comprehensive reference to search engine optimization, from how search engines work to technical, content and link strategy.

title: SEO for Growth
author: John Jantsch & Phil Singleton
about: SEO explained for marketers and business owners, tying search strategy to content and business goals.

title: Product-Led SEO
author: Eli Schwartz
about: Schwartz's argument that SEO should be built around products and user needs rather than keywords and tactics.

title: Digital Marketing Strategy
author: Simon Kingsnorth
about: An integrated approach to planning digital marketing, covering the channels, the measurement and how they fit together.

title: The Intelligent Investor
author: Benjamin Graham
about: Graham's guide to value investing and to the temperament of the defensive investor. Warren Buffett has called it the best book on investing ever written.

title: Financial Intelligence for Entrepreneurs
author: Karen Berman & Joe Knight
about: How to read financial statements and understand what the numbers say about a business, written for founders rather than accountants.

title: The Paytech Book
author: Susanne Chishti et al. (eds.)
about: Essays from practitioners on the technology reshaping payments.

title: Practical Business Math
author: Jeffrey Slater
about: A textbook on the mathematics of business: percentages, interest, discounts, payroll and financial statements.

title: Same as Ever
author: Morgan Housel
about: Short essays on the things that do not change: human behavior around risk, greed, fear and opportunity.

title: Poor Charlie's Almanack
author: Charles Munger
about: Munger's talks and thinking, including his latticework of mental models and his speech on the psychology of human misjudgment.

title: The Great Mental Models
author: Shane Parrish
about: The first volume of Farnam Street's series on general thinking tools such as first principles, inversion and second-order thinking.

title: Super Thinking
author: Gabriel Weinberg & Lauren McCann
about: A large catalogue of mental models from across disciplines, organized for practical use.

title: The Personal MBA
author: Josh Kaufman
about: A self-education in business fundamentals, distilled from hundreds of books into a set of core concepts.

title: Notes from Underground
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
edition: Vintage, translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky
about: A bitter, self-lacerating narrator rejects the idea that reason and self-interest can explain human beings. The book that opens the door to existentialism.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
edition: Vintage, translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky
about: A poor student murders a pawnbroker to prove a theory about extraordinary men, then cannot live with it. Dostoevsky's great novel of guilt and redemption.

title: The Idiot
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
edition: Vintage, translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky
about: Dostoevsky's attempt to portray a truly good man, Prince Myshkin, and what happens when goodness meets the society around it.

title: Demons
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
edition: Vintage, translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky
about: A provincial town is torn apart by a radical cell, based on a real political murder. A warning about ideas that consume the people who hold them.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
edition: Vintage, translated by Richard Pevear and Larissa Volokhonsky
about: Three brothers, a murdered father and the question of whether everything is permitted if there is no God. Dostoevsky's last and largest novel.

title: Short Fiction
author: Leo Tolstoy
edition: Norton Critical Edition, edited by Michael R. Katz, 2nd edition
about: Tolstoy's shorter works, including The Death of Ivan Ilyich, with contextual and critical material.

title: Hadji Murad
author: Leo Tolstoy
edition: Modern Library, translated by Aylmer Maude, introduction by Azar Nafisi
about: Tolstoy's late short novel about a Chechen warrior caught between the Russian empire and his own leader, published after Tolstoy's death.

title: Cancer Ward
author: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
about: Patients in a Soviet cancer ward in the 1950s, among them a former labor camp prisoner, confront illness and the system that shaped their lives.

title: Dead Souls
author: Nikolai Gogol
edition: NYRB Classics, translated by Donald Rayfield
about: A swindler travels provincial Russia buying up dead serfs who still exist on paper. Gogol's comic, unfinished masterpiece.

title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
edition: Penguin Classics Deluxe, translated by Norman Denny
about: Hugo's vast novel of Jean Valjean, a convict pursued by the law across decades of French history, and of mercy set against justice.

title: The Stranger
author: Albert Camus
edition: Vintage International, translated by Matthew Ward
about: Meursault kills a man on a beach and is condemned less for the crime than for his indifference. Camus's first novel of the absurd.

title: The Plague
author: Albert Camus
about: An epidemic seals off an Algerian city, and its people respond with courage, denial and solidarity. Often read as an allegory of occupation and of any shared catastrophe.

title: Candide
author: Voltaire
edition: Penguin Classics, translated by Theo Cuffe, and the Norton Critical Edition
about: Voltaire's satire of philosophical optimism, following a naive young man through disaster after disaster. It ends in the advice to cultivate our garden.

title: The Magic Mountain
author: Thomas Mann
edition: Oxford World's Classics, translated by Simon Pare
about: A young man visits a sanatorium in the Swiss Alps for three weeks and stays seven years. Mann's novel of time, illness and European ideas before the First World War.

title: Demian
author: Hermann Hesse
about: A young man's awakening under the influence of a mysterious friend, and his break from the respectable world he was raised in.

title: The World of Yesterday
author: Stefan Zweig
about: Zweig's memoir of the cultured, secure Europe he grew up in and its destruction, finished shortly before his death in exile.

title: The Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
about: Gregor Samsa wakes to find himself transformed into a monstrous insect, and his family's response becomes the real subject.

title: Satantango
author: László Krasznahorkai
edition: New Directions, translated by George Szirtes
about: A decaying Hungarian collective farm awaits the return of a man thought dead, in long, spiraling sentences. Krasznahorkai's first novel.

title: Lolita
author: Vladimir Nabokov
about: Narrated by Humbert Humbert, an eloquent and self-justifying abuser. A study of how beautiful language can be used to disguise monstrous acts.

title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
author: Ernest Hemingway
about: An American volunteer is sent to blow up a bridge during the Spanish Civil War. Hemingway's longest novel, about three days and a whole life.

title: The Old Man and the Sea
author: Ernest Hemingway
about: An aging Cuban fisherman hooks a great marlin and fights it for days. Short, spare and central to Hemingway's Nobel Prize.

title: The Complete Short Stories
author: Ernest Hemingway
about: The collected stories, including previously unpublished work, where Hemingway's compression is at its sharpest.

title: The Road
author: Cormac McCarthy
about: A father and son walk across a burned America toward the coast. McCarthy's bleakest landscape and his most tender book. It won the Pulitzer Prize.

title: Sabbath's Theater
author: Philip Roth
about: A disgraced puppeteer spirals through grief and appetite. Roth's most outrageous novel and, for many readers, his best. It won the National Book Award.

title: A Little Life
author: Hanya Yanagihara
about: Four friends in New York across several decades, centered on one man whose past will not let him go. A long, harrowing novel about friendship and suffering.

title: The Goldfinch
author: Donna Tartt
about: A boy survives a museum bombing that kills his mother and keeps a small Dutch painting that shapes the rest of his life. It won the Pulitzer Prize.

title: House of Leaves
author: Mark Z. Danielewski
about: A house that is larger on the inside than the outside, told through footnotes, found documents and typography that becomes part of the story.

title: Middlemarch
author: George Eliot
about: The lives of an English provincial town, above all Dorothea Brooke's. Often called the greatest English novel for its moral intelligence and range.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
about: The passion between Heathcliff and Catherine and the damage it does across two generations on the Yorkshire moors.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
edition: Belknap Press of Harvard University Press, edited by Nicholas Frankel
about: A young man stays beautiful while his portrait ages and corrupts. This edition restores the uncensored text Wilde first submitted, with Frankel's annotations.

title: The Return of the Native
author: Thomas Hardy
about: Passion and restlessness on Egdon Heath, a landscape Hardy makes into a character of its own.

title: The Divine Comedy
author: Dante Alighieri
edition: Translated by Robert and Jean Hollander, three volumes
about: Dante's journey through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise. The Hollander translation carries extensive commentary drawn from centuries of scholarship.

title: Paradise Lost
author: John Milton
edition: Penguin Classics, edited by John Leonard
about: Milton's epic of the fall of Satan and of humankind, written to justify the ways of God to men. Satan is its most memorable figure.

title: The Iliad and The Odyssey
author: Homer
about: The two foundational epics of the West: the wrath of Achilles at Troy and Odysseus's long voyage home.

title: The Aeneid
author: Virgil
edition: Penguin Classics Deluxe, translated by Robert Fagles
about: Virgil's epic of Aeneas fleeing Troy to found the people who would become Rome, written under Augustus.

title: The Riverside Shakespeare
author: G. Blakemore Evans (ed.)
about: The complete works in a single scholarly volume, with introductions and textual notes. A standard edition for decades.

title: Metamorphoses
author: Ovid
about: Some two hundred and fifty myths of transformation, linked from the creation of the world to the deification of Julius Caesar. A source for Western art and literature ever since.

title: Rhetoric
author: Aristotle
edition: Penguin Classics, translated by Hugh Lawson-Tancred
about: Aristotle's analysis of persuasion through character, emotion and argument. Still the foundation of how rhetoric is taught.

title: Collected Fictions
author: Jorge Luis Borges
about: All of Borges's fiction in one volume: labyrinths, infinite libraries, imaginary books and mirrors.

title: Selected Non-Fictions
author: Jorge Luis Borges
about: Borges's essays, reviews and lectures, as strange and brilliant as his stories.

subsection: Crime, mystery, and the propulsive shelf
title: In the Woods
author: Tana French
about: A Dublin detective investigates a child's murder in the woods where, as a boy, he survived something he cannot remember. French's first novel.

subsection: Crime, mystery, and the propulsive shelf
title: Stone's Fall
author: Iain Pears
about: A financier's death investigated backward through three narratives across Europe and decades, in a novel about money, espionage and secrets.

subsection: Crime, mystery, and the propulsive shelf
title: Wrong Place Wrong Time
author: Gillian McAllister
about: A mother watches her son commit a murder, then wakes each day further back in time, working backward to find what led to it.

subsection: Crime, mystery, and the propulsive shelf
title: Carter Beats the Devil
author: Glen David Gold
about: A novel about Charles Carter, a stage magician in 1920s America, drawn into a mystery when a president dies suddenly after attending his show.

title: The Culture novels
author: Iain M. Banks
about: Banks's series about the Culture, a post-scarcity civilization run by benevolent artificial minds, told mostly through the people at its edges.
